record.original_question: Do there exist wandering domains for complex Henon maps?

evidence.quote: Problem 10.2.1 Do there exist wandering domains for complex Henon maps?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A complex Hénon map is a polynomial automorphism of $\mathbb{C}^2$ of the form
$$H(x,y) = (p(x) - a y,\; x),$$
where $p \in \mathbb{C}[x]$ is a polynomial of degree at least $2$ and $a \in \mathbb{C}^*$. The Fatou set $F(H)$ of $H$ is the largest open subset of $\mathbb{C}^2$ on which the family of iterates $\{H^n\}_{n\geq 0}$ is locally equicontinuous (equivalently, a normal family). The connected components of $F(H)$ are called Fatou components. A Fatou component $U$ is called a wandering domain if $H^m(U) \cap H^n(U) = \emptyset$ for all integers $m \neq n \geq 0$ (so that $U$ is not eventually periodic).

Question: Does there exist a complex Hénon map (i.e., some choice of $p$ and $a$ as above) that possesses a wandering Fatou component?
artifact.status_search_result: The question was answered affirmatively. Berger and Biebler proved the existence of wandering Fatou components (wandering domains) for complex Hénon maps, in sharp contrast to Sullivan's no-wandering-domains theorem in one complex dimension. This is recorded in recent surveys of open problems on Hénon maps as a now-resolved problem.

status_evidence.title: Hénon maps: a list of open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys recent progress including the construction by Berger–Biebler of wandering Fatou components for complex Hénon maps.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of wandering domains for complex Hénon maps has been established.

status_evidence.title: Dynamics of Hénon maps: real, complex and beyond (BIRS report)
status_evidence.snippet: Reports on the construction of wandering Fatou components for complex Hénon maps, contrasting with Sullivan's theorem in dimension one.
status_evidence.claim: Wandering domains for complex Hénon maps have been constructed.
